rules.when: Mechanical work whose every edit the brief dictates, with no judgment left: a rename, formatting sweep, typo fix, version or pin bump, single setting flip, deleting or moving named files or sections, copying an existing file verbatim, removing tool-generated leftovers, or gathering files. Any number of files fits.

Clearly specified implementation work of ordinary size, about 150 changed lines or fewer of new or rewritten logic: a specified feature, a bug fix whose cause the brief points to, tests for existing behavior, or applying a pattern the brief names (a worked example, a pilot pull request, a sibling repository) to more places. The worker makes only local choices. Repeating one known change across many files or workflows, deleting the code it replaces, and running proof or CI checks to confirm it all stay here.

Clearly specified implementation work above about 150 changed lines of new or rewritten logic, staying within one program, where the brief already settles the design: a new feature, option, check or command carried through code, schema, docs and tests, a fix that first needs a new reproduction harness, or a refactor across several modules along a design the brief states. An upstream sync into a fork is sized by the conflicts it must resolve, not by the incoming diff.

Implementation that needs real design judgment or must keep many interacting parts consistent: design decisions the brief leaves open, a feature spanning several processes, machines or services, new code that stores, passes or guards secrets or credentials, a risky refactor of shared state, concurrency or migration logic, coordinating several workers, visual or interaction design without a settled target, or a large rebuild an earlier attempt failed at. File count, proof runs and CI edits alone do not qualify; a known change applied by a named pattern takes a smaller rule.
Bounded investigation, audit, diagnosis, triage, reproduction, or planning that produces a report rather than a code change: a scout, a survey of issues, a root-cause hunt, an evaluation of options.

A code change whose cause or scope is not yet known: a bug, flaky check, environment-only failure, or unexplained regression that must first be diagnosed across systems, processes or machines before the fix is clear. A fix the brief already locates takes a smaller rule.

Work that must run on this Mac against its live configuration (terminal, Herdr, WezTerm, pi setup or home network) and changes or proves that live state. A repository change that only targets Mac software and is proved in its isolated copy takes the size rules.
